correctness.rationale: For plant neighborhood A with x=|U\A|, extinction is uniform surviving 2-subset of U\A and P(E_A)=binom(x,2)/binom(N,2). For pair A,B, let z=|U\(A∪B)|, and independence reduces exactly to binom(z,2)binom(N,2)=binom(x,2)binom(y,2), 2≤x≤y<N and max(2,x+y−N)≤z≤x. Independently exhaustively enumerate all these integer cardinality tuples for N=3..10: none at N=3..8; N=9 unique (4,4,2); N=10 unique (3,6,2). Consequently at 9 all |A|=5 and |A∩B|=3; triple common-core t forces each pair-only 3−t, each plant-only t−1, unused 3−t, so exactly t∈{1,2,3}. All 36 survivor pairs give marginal 6/36, pair 1/36, triple [1,0,0]/36, unlike (1/6)^3; no unused pollinators forces t=3. At N=10 every independent pair requires sizes (3,6) of complements, impossible for three plants as odd triangle cannot be properly two-colored. The finite search is mathematically exhaustive because its integer parameters cover all subsets; no infinite extrapolation.
residual_risks: Only exactly two uniformly sampled survivors and three nondegenerate plant extinction events; no random heterogeneous removal or other survivor quota.
